data.description:
# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`
in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) invalidates a stored audit when any
fingerprint component changes. The original formulation fingerprinted
**whole-repo** state (git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files +
whole-repo working-tree hash), so any commit or uncommitted/untracked change
anywhere in the repository — even one from an *unrelated* work item — invalidated
every stored audit and re-triggered the full audit pipeline.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD
`310773d5`; afterwards an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged
`aaabdede` to dev, the fingerprint changed (`58947e06…` matched recomputation at
`310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), the re-audit ran and blocked on the pre-flight
full-suite cache gate — a verified item stuck in review.

**Current state (2026-10-21, HEAD `fe85415a3`):** the whole-repo components have
**already been replaced** by per-touched-file scoping (SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, done):
the payload is now `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` where each
touched path contributes its committed state (blob hash at HEAD, else the latest
touching commit) plus its narrowed working-tree state. An unrelated commit or
working-tree change now invalidates **only if it touches a file in the item's
touched set** (commits referencing the item id + comment-recorded commit hashes +
Key Files). The whole-repo HEAD sha is no longer a component, and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` no longer exists. The observed failure case is
therefore **no longer reproducible** with today's formula.

The remaining delta of this item is the **strict rule** recorded in the original
Q&A: "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data
AFTER the audit was created." That rule is stronger than the current
per-touched-file formula — it requires a fingerprint over the item's own data
only (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git
calls**, so even a committed/uncommitted change to a file this item touched does
not invalidate.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness
  short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid
unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity
(including changes to files this item happened to touch) doesn't invalidate my
audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data
   only** — title + description (description contains the ACs and the Key Files
   section). The per-path git components (committed HEAD blob hashes, working-tree
   state) and the whole-repo HEAD component are **removed** from the fingerprint
   — **no git calls in the computation** (`_resolve_touched_files` /
   `_compute_path_fingerprints` are no longer used by the fingerprint).
   *(PENDING producer decision — see OPEN QUESTION in Appendix.)*
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate
   a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test:
   fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored
   audit — **including changes to files the item itself touched** (stricter than
   the current per-touched-path formula). Regression test: fingerprint is stable
   across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences and
   across touched-file edits.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files
   section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing
   description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do
   **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content). This
   also removes the current comment-recorded-commit-hash contribution to the
   touched set (SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L) — the fingerprint must not depend on comments.
6. **Migration of legacy reports:** reports persisted before this change carry
   fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formulas that cannot be recomputed.
   Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`)
   so legacy/unversioned lines are distinguishable; legacy/unversioned reports
   fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt +
   `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`, plus the persist-write tolerance) — **no
   silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the
   one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after
   the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: after the simplification, remove the fingerprints-only
   git machinery no longer referenced elsewhere (verify each of
   `_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` — those still used by
   the file-scope manifest and Phase 2 remain). `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
   (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ) is **already removed**; `_resolve_audited_head` stays
   (still used by green-run attestation).
8. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate
   section, currently ~lines 248-318/579-594/699/816), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
   (~lines 42/182-186/204-210), and the code docstrings on
   `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` /
   `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. All fingerprint call sites that must keep
   working with the simplified formula: `_check_audit_freshness` (item gate),
   `_get_child_audit_verdict` + `_child_content_changed` (child reuse, LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR),
   `cmd_check_freshness` (read-only probe, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI),
   `_run_remediation_loop` (ruff-config re-hash), `_phase_fetch_and_cq`,
   `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children`, `_phase_children` (child audit persistence).
   Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is
  reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the
  gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make
  any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still
  short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved); the read-only
  `check-freshness` probe and `isAuditFresh` (ship, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI) keep
  working.
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls
  through to a full re-audit (existing behaviour).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse uses the same fingerprint — it must keep
  working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~2412) — payload =
    `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` (per-touched-path, SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P).
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~1950) — content gate primary; time gate
    (60 s + persist-write tolerance ~30 s) floor for fingerprint-less legacy
    reports; persistence-write tolerance covers the runner's own writes
    (SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM).
  - `_extract_content_fingerprint` (line ~2073) — parses the unversioned line.
  - `_resolve_touched_files` (line ~2213), `_compute_path_fingerprints`
    (line ~2336) — the per-touched-path git machinery this item's strict rule
    removes from the fingerprint (verify remaining uses: file-scope manifest at
    ~5224/7964/10897).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line ~1112,
    unversioned); embedded at ~5721/5747/6172 (persist) + re-extracted by the gate.
  - Call sites of the fingerprint: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020),
    `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_child_content_changed` (~7009),
    `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120), `_phase_gate` (~9466),
    `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357),
    `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11380/11516/11918).
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` — **already removed** (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ
    component replaced by per-path state); `_resolve_audited_head` (~2852) stays.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — tests split across files; fingerprint/freshness coverage
  lives mainly in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (1336 lines:
  `TestTouchedFileResolution` ~190, `TestContentFreshnessGate` ~348 — incl.
  `test_fingerprint_payload_keys_exclude_global_head`, touched-file invalidation
  tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`, comment-hash tests) and
  `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`. Some existing tests assert the
  per-touched-path invalidation behaviour that this item reverses
  (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` /
  `..._dirty` / `..._staged`, tool-artefact invalidation, comment-contribution
  tests, `test_child_content_changed_fresh_survives_unrelated_head_movement` —
  these must be updated to the new rule).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section ~lines 248-254
  (content gate + time gate + fail-open), 292/309-318 (child reuse), 579/594
  (inherited pass / child reuse), 699/816 (Phase 2 child reuse).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary ~lines 42, 182-186, 204-210.
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side
  `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based
  `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this;
  covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog). The ship-side
  `isAuditFresh` consumption is SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI (done) and stays in scope
  only as a consumer that must keep working.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`
  (simplify to item-data-only), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_extract_content_fingerprint`
  (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, dead-git-
  machinery removal, docstrings
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — update
  fingerprint/freshness tests to the new rule
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary lines

## Related work

- `SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P` — Audit freshness: re-audit only when files touched by
  the work item changed (**done**, 2026-09-28) — implemented the per-touched-path
  formula currently in the code; this item's strict rule goes further (item-data-
  only, zero git). **The original observed failure is already fixed by this item.**
- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content
  fingerprint (**done**, not in_review as the original brief stated) — the
  whole-repo working-tree component this item's rule REMOVES (superseded; the
  per-path state it inspired is also removed by this strict rule).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (**done**) —
  introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L` — Stabilise child freshness fingerprint comments
  (**done**, 2026-10-21) — comment-recorded commit hashes feed the touched set;
  this item's rule removes the comment dependency (AC5).
- `SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI` — Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint
  (**done**) — read-only `check-freshness` probe consumer that must keep working.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (**done**) —
  the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item
  (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern,
  out of scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files
  section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content
  and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy/unversioned reports fall
  back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy
  item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a
  v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD/working-tree churn thereafter.
  Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence (now broader):** dropping the per-path git
  components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it — not
  just via another work item's Key-File edit, but **any committed or uncommitted
  change to a file this item touched** (the protection deliberately added by
  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ and kept by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, with tests asserting the
  invalidation). Accepted by design per the recorded rule; the audit's verdict
  remains the record for the item's own data. **This reversal is the OPEN
  QUESTION pending producer confirmation.**
- **Scope-creep risk:** reversing the per-touched-path design re-touches the
  child-reuse gate, the read-only probe, and the ship-side `isAuditFresh`
  consumer. Keep those as consumers that must keep working — do not extend the
  item to re-design them.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for
  items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits
  ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out
  of scope (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit?
  — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to
  this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer:
  remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item
  supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per
  rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit
  decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the
  fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing
  time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.

**OPEN QUESTION (2026-10-21 intake re-check; needs producer review before the
ACs are finalised):** The original trigger — unrelated whole-repo churn
invalidating audits — is **already fixed** by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P (per-touched-
path fingerprint, done 2026-09-28, after the original Q&A was recorded). The
strict item-data-only formula in AC1/AC3 would additionally remove the
per-touched-file protection (committed/uncommitted changes to files the item
touched no longer invalidate), reversing tested behaviour shipped in
SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P / SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ. Options: (a) proceed with the strict
formula as originally recorded (preferred — matches the recorded rule verbatim;
the stale-code-evidence trade-off is already accepted above); (b) narrow this
item to the uncontroversial remainder (versioned fingerprint line + legacy
time-gate migration + docs + dead-code tidy, keeping per-touched-path state). Ask
to be re-answered via: `wl comment add SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 --comment "answer: ..."`.
Research: inspected `_compute_content_fingerprint`/`_check_audit_freshness`/
`_extract_content_fingerprint` at HEAD `fe85415a3`; confirmed whole-repo HEAD and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` are gone and the payload is `{path_states,
description_hash, key_files}`; confirmed per-touched-path invalidation tests
exist in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`.
data.title: Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change

## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).
data.title: Audit runner: filter non-Python files before passing to ruff

## Summary

While shipping LLM-proxy v0.1.19, the ship wrapper was invoked with an unrecognised flag (to read help). It **ran the entire post-release sequence without performing a release**, closing 74 real release-candidate work items with the previous release's reason (`Shipped in v0.1.18`). The real release then found zero candidates and produced an empty changelog. Full incident: llm worklog **LP-0MUEALIM60037F1S**.

## Root cause

1. **No argument validation in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`.** Only `--skip-checks` is wrapper-only; every other flag (including `--help`) is forwarded to `merge-dev-to-main.sh`.
2. **`merge-dev-to-main.sh` treats `-h|--help` as usage and `exit 0`** — so the child succeeds without releasing.
3. **`runReleaseImpl` does not detect the no-op release.** It skips the PR wait (no PR URL), runs a no-op `syncDevWithMain()`, then resolves `version` from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` — the **previous** tag.
4. **`verifyReleaseMerge(version)` only checks** that the tag exists on `origin` and is an ancestor of `origin/main`. The previous tag already satisfies this, so the guard passes.
5. **`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` then closes every `stage=in_review` item with the wrong reason.**

## Overlap resolution (duplicate check, Step 4.3)

Steps 1–4 and 5's *close* trigger were fixed by the overlapping, now-completed
work item **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** ("ship: run-release.js --help runs
post-release steps and closes items against a stale tag") and its children
SA-0MV13B5F8005NT6G (fail-fast CLI), SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA (newly-created-tag
gate) and SA-0MV13B4YT0093CKT (regression tests). Verified in the current tree:

- `parseReleaseArgs()` + `runRelease()` reject unknown flags (exit 13) and make
  `--help`/`-h` fully inert (usage, exit 0) before the Code Freeze marker or any
  gate runs.
- `snapshotReleaseTags()` / `isNewlyCreatedTag()` gate every post-release step:
  a tag that already existed before the run exits 14 without closing anything.

The remaining, still-unmet gap from the original criteria is **idempotency of
the close sweep**: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` unconditionally re-issues
`wl close --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` for every candidate, so a repeated
post-release run (or an item already annotated for this version by an earlier
sweep) is re-closed and re-annotated — the 99 spurious close comments / 25
double-closed items observed in the incident. This work item now covers that
gap only.

## Desired behaviour / Acceptance Criteria (remaining gap)

- [ ] AC1: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` skips any candidate that already carries a close marker for **this** version (`Shipped in v<version>`), with **no** `wl close` and **no** additional comment/annotation for that item; the skipped items are reported in the return value.
- [ ] AC2: The marker match is version-exact — `Shipped in v0.1.1` must not match version `0.1.18` (and vice versa); markers for other versions do not suppress a close.
- [ ] AC3: Reading the existing markers is injectable/fail-safe: an unreadable comment source logs a warning and leaves the existing close behaviour intact (a release is never blocked by the idempotency check); no test touches the live worklog.
- [ ] AC4: Regression tests cover (a) a re-run of the post-release close does not duplicate `wl close` calls or comments, (b) an item carrying another version's marker is still closed, (c) version-exact matching, (d) the unreadable-marker fail-safe path.
- [ ] AC5: Full test suite passes; `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / reference docs describe the idempotency guarantee.

## Key files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` (marker check), new pure helper for version-exact marker detection.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — regression tests.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — documentation.

## Already delivered by SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR (not re-implemented here)

- `--help`/`-h` inert; unknown flags rejected non-zero before any post-release step.
- `verifyReleaseMerge` alone is insufficient — a newly-created-tag gate now
  proves *this* run produced the release tag.
- Post-release close/notify/cleanup skipped whenever no new tag was created.
data.title: run-release.js runs post-release steps without a release: unknown flags forwarded, verifyReleaseMerge accepts the previous tag

# Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote snapshot-exempt children

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B (ContextHub) — canonicalised here because this repository owns the audit skill.
**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high · **Recurrence of:** SA-0MUJAPC680078396 (completed) and SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ (completed)
**RCA:** `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md`

## Problem statement

A parent audit running in **separate-process child mode** (`--no-child-in-main-slot`) demoted **all 11** of its children from `completed`/`in_review` to `open`/`blocked` at `plan_complete`, at the exact timestamps their child audits were persisted. F1 and F8 (the two dependency-free children) were set to `open`; the other nine cascaded to `blocked` through the dependency chain. The parent's own verdict then read `Ready to close: No` with the sole blocker being those now-`plan_complete` children, even though all six of its own acceptance criteria were `met`/`adjusted`.

This is the side-effect demotion that SA-0MUJAPC680078396 explicitly forbids and that SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ was meant to prevent ('infra-fallback verdicts must never demote').

## Root cause (proven)

`_persist_child_audit()` persists child audits through `persist_audit.py`, which calls:

    wl audit-set <child> --ready-to-close no

and `wl audit-set` with a negative verdict calls `db.revertToPlanComplete(child)` (`src/commands/audit-result.ts:207-214`; `packages/shared` `database.revertToPlanComplete`), which unconditionally rewrites `completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete`.

Two invariants are therefore bypassed:

1. **The audited item's lifecycle guards.** `ac_fallback_used` (SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ) and `_cascade_suppress_demotion` (SA-0MUJAPC680078396) live in `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` for the *item under audit*. `persist_audit` → `audit-set` is a skill-unaware primitive and consults neither.
2. **The child-exemption snapshot.** `_child_is_exempt` is only consulted by the runner's own closure checks, not by `audit-set`.

Measured: 8 of 11 children were persisted with `readyToClose=false` (`wl audit-show --json`) and every one was reverted; the 3 with `true` were not. Dependency cascade then produced the 9 `blocked` states.

**Aggravating factor.** Those child verdicts were infra-fallback-tainted: `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7`, with 5 of 11 child Phase-1 screens landing exactly on the 600 s `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT` cap. Per SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ an infra-fallback 'No' is not an explicit model assessment and must take the **restore** path — but `audit-set` has no notion of fallback provenance, so tainted verdicts demote.

**Open sub-question (to confirm in this item).** The parent's closure reported those children as blocking even though they were `in_review` at audit start and `_capture_exempt_children_snapshot` should have exempted them. `all_children_reviewed` honours `snapshot_exempt` (audit_runner.py ~5633) but the report's `not_reviewed` text path (~5759) does **not**, so text and verdict can disagree. Determine whether the snapshot was empty (children already demoted pre-snapshot), lost, or simply not applied to the text path.

## User stories

- **Audit operator** — As an operator, I want a parent audit to leave the lifecycle of children that were `in_review` at audit start untouched, so a read-only run never pushes completed work back into the actionable queue.
- **Release manager** — As a release manager, I want `blocked` never to cascade through a dependency chain as a side effect of an audit, so a release gate cannot be stalled by an audit artefact.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want infra-fallback child verdicts to be recorded as `partial` diagnostics, never as lifecycle-changing 'No's.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A child audit persisted by a parent run (both child-audit modes) **cannot** change a child's status/stage when the child was `completed`/`in_review` at audit start: `_persist_child_audit`/`persist_audit` either writes the audit without the `audit-set` reversion side effect, or the runner restores the captured pre-audit status/stage immediately after persisting.
2. Infra-fallback-tainted child verdicts (parse failure, timeout, provider error, concurrency limit) never demote any item — the same rule SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ applies to the audited item now applies to children persisted by a parent.
3. No `blocked` status may be introduced on any work item as a side effect of an audit run; verified by a regression test asserting the full child set's status/stage is byte-identical before and after a parent audit.
4. The parent's closure decision and its report text use the **same** exemption source: `not_reviewed` (~5759) honours `snapshot_exempt`, so a parent whose children were all `in_review` at audit start reports `Ready to close: Yes` when its own ACs pass.
5. A regression test covers the observed scenario end to end (parent + N children, all `in_review`, child verdicts `No` and tainted): children end `completed`/`in_review`, parent verdict `Yes`, no `blocked`.
6. `skill/audit/tests/` passes, including the new tests.

## Evidence

ContextHub run log: `~/.audit_debug/ContextHub/audit-WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B-2nd-20261021-102346.log` (9312 s; `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7`). Child `readyToClose` values and the pre/post lifecycle states are reproducible from the child items under `WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B`.

## RCA CORRECTION (2026-10-21) — read before implementing

**This supersedes AC4 and part of the RCA's original F3 as written.** The RCA doc has been corrected (commit 210f3d008, `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md` §5).

**Disproven:** the earlier claim that `not_reviewed` (~L5759) ignores `snapshot_exempt` and therefore contradicts the verdict. Every `not_reviewed` reference (~L5780, ~L5811-5815, ~L5827-5830) is inside the **No** branch, so it cannot drive the verdict. Do not implement that.

**Verified mechanism instead — F3a:** `all_ac_acceptable` (~L5609-5621) folds **child AC verdicts** into the parent's closure with **no** `_child_is_exempt` filter:

```python
child_acs = [a for c in child_results if (...) for a in c.get("ac_results", [])]
all_ac_acceptable = all(r["verdict"] in _ACCEPTABLE_VERDICTS for r in ac_results + child_acs)
```

So a snapshot-exempt child that was re-screened as a side effect into `partial` (infra-fallback/timeout) still forces `Ready to close: No`. This is exactly what happened: all 11 children were `in_review` at audit start, all six parent ACs were `met`/`adjusted`, and the verdict was `No` purely from timeout-tainted `partial` child ACs. The exemption-aware checks that follow (`all_children_reviewed` ~L5633, `any_child_audit_not_ready` ~L5643) are defeated by the aggregation that precedes them.

**F3b (misattribution):** because parent `unmet_count` and `partial_count` are both 0, the report prints "N children not yet in in_review/done stage" (~L5827-5830) — blaming the children's **stages** when the driver was their **AC verdicts**. The report must name the real blocker plus its fallback provenance.

**Why the existing test misses it:** `test_audit_runner_review.py::TestChildExemptionSnapshot::test_snapshot_keeps_parent_yes_when_child_demoted` passes a demoted child with `child_audit_ready=False` but **no `ac_results`**, so the AC-aggregation path is never exercised. Extend the test with tainted child ACs.

**Coordination:** `dev` was red at 2026-10-21T15:22 with 5 audit-skill failures in exactly these paths — `TestChildExemptionSnapshot::test_report_text_honours_snapshot_for_not_reviewed_children` and four `test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` cases (pending gate, 2× unserviced main-slot verdicts, interactive re-run). Reconcile with any in-flight change before rewriting these paths.

data.comment: Related finding (2026-10-21): the 600s cap is not only a wall-clock cost — it is the *input* to a lifecycle bug. 7 timeout-tainted child ACs became `partial` verdicts that then forced the parent to 'Ready to close: No' (see SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ F3a: child ACs are folded into the parent's closure with no exemption filter) and 8 tainted child 'No' verdicts demoted 11 in_review children. So this item's AC3 (quarantine capped-screen verdicts, surface child_screen_timeouts) is a prerequisite for trusting any child-level verdict, not just a performance nicety. Full RCA: docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md (Sections 4 and 5).
